title: Malcolm the 'Last to Come, First to Leave' Otter
outlineDescription: Teaches managers how to document employee performance accurately. Includes scenarios of poor performance and how to document these behaviours with factual evidence.

sceneParts.narrativeText:
You are the supervisor of the Operations Team at the Red Cross.

Every otter employee is expected to report to work by 9:00 AM.

For the past two weeks, Malcolm has been arriving around 10:30 AM every day.

Today, Malcolm walks into the office holding his coffee while the rest of the team is already inside meetings.

You notice:
• No prior notice was given
• Malcolm immediately starts casual conversations
• At exactly 6:00 PM, he leaves on time every day

As supervisor, HR requires you to formally document this performance issue.

A HR notification appears on your screen:

"Reminder: Formal documentation required for repeated attendance issues."

sceneParts.questionText: Task 1: How should you fill in the Incident Details section?
sceneParts.contextHintText: HR documentation requires specific, measurable details to be considered valid evidence.

choices.label: A
choices.feedbackText: Too vague. HR documentation requires measurable details such as specific dates and times.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Employee arrived between 10:20 AM – 10:35 AM from 29 April – 13 May 2026 despite scheduled reporting time of 9:00 AM.
choices.feedbackText: Good documentation includes specific dates and timings that can be verified.

sceneParts.questionText: Task 2: What supporting evidence should you attach?
sceneParts.contextHintText: Evidence must be objective and verifiable, not based on personal memory.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I remember seeing him late every day.
choices.feedbackText: Personal memory is not reliable evidence. Use objective records that can be independently verified.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attendance records and meeting logs attached.
choices.feedbackText: Always support documentation with objective evidence such as attendance screenshots or system records.

sceneParts.questionText: Task 3: How should you describe the operational impact?
sceneParts.contextHintText: Focus on how the behaviour affects work operations, not on the employee's character.

choices.label: A
choices.feedbackText: Avoid personal judgements. Focus on how the behaviour affects work operations rather than attacking character.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeated lateness delayed meeting discussions and affected project coordination.
choices.feedbackText: Focus on how behaviour affects work operations instead of attacking the employee personally.

sceneParts.questionText: Task 4: What should you write in the Manager Comments section?
sceneParts.contextHintText: Use neutral and professional wording. Avoid assumptions or emotional language.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Malcolm clearly does not care about work.
choices.feedbackText: Avoid assumptions about intent or emotions. Stick to observable, documented facts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Employee did not provide prior notice regarding repeated late arrivals.
choices.feedbackText: Use neutral and professional wording. Avoid assumptions or emotional language.

sceneParts.narrativeText:
The HR documentation form is now fully completed.

All sections have been filled with specific, objective, and professional information.

✔ Include dates and timings
✔ Focus on observable behaviour
✔ Attach supporting evidence
✔ Explain operational impact
✔ Use professional and neutral wording
✘ Avoid opinions and assumptions

Documentation completed.

Next Step: Conduct employee feedback discussion.

A calendar meeting invitation has been drafted:
"Meeting with Malcolm – Attendance Discussion"

Suggested conversation starters:

• "I noticed you've been arriving after reporting hours recently."
• "Is there anything affecting your attendance?"
• "I'd like to understand if there are any challenges we should be aware of."

Questions to explore during the feedback session:

• Are there personal or operational challenges affecting punctuality?
• Does the employee understand attendance expectations?
• Is additional support required?
• What improvement plan can be agreed upon moving forward?

Malcolm and the supervisor sit together professionally in a meeting room.

Malcolm appears more serious and attentive while the supervisor speaks calmly.

Final Learning Points:

• Document facts, not emotions
• Use evidence and specific details
• Explain operational impact clearly
• Remain objective and professional
• Conduct respectful feedback discussions
